prompt:
You describe a graph or chart from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. What is plotted against what: for each axis, the quantity, the unit and the range (first and last tick labels).
2. Each curve or series: its label or condition (temperature, voltage, mode, ...) and its overall trend in words.
3. Values printed in the figure as text (annotations, labelled points, legend values). Do not estimate values from where a curve sits; if a value is not printed, describe the trend in words instead.

Figure type: graph or chart
Section: 4 PCB placement guideline based on magnetic influences > 4.5 Hard magnetic offsets > Soft magnetic effects
Caption: Figure 14: Quantifying soft magnetic distortion
Text inside the figure (exact, from the PDF text layer): Ideal measurement data on | a circle | BX | BY | BX | BY | Major ellipse | axis | Measured | data | Anisotropic distortion due to | soft magnetic effects | Minor ellipse | axis
Text that mentions the figure: The usage of soft magnetic materials close to the geomagnetic sensor must be avoided. The presence of soft magnetic materials at the sensor can be estimated by rotating the PCB on a nonmagnetic table (free of iron). Ideally, the measured data points will all be in a circle. In usual cases, soft magnetic effects are visible as distortion of this circle into an ellipse as visible in Figure 14.

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".

answer.text:
Graph of magnetic field components.
The horizontal axis is labeled BX and has no units or tick labels visible.
The vertical axis is labeled BY and has no units or tick labels visible.

There are two main plots:
The left plot is labeled "Ideal measurement data on a circle". It shows "Measured data" represented by blue 'x' marks forming a circle.
The right plot is labeled "Anisotropic distortion due to soft magnetic effects". It shows a shape distorted from a circle into an ellipse. This shape is composed of "Measured data" (blue 'x' marks), a "Major ellipse" (dashed line), and a "Minor ellipse" (solid orange line).
